chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I asked him about a man who prays in a corner of the room, and his wife or his daughter prays beside him in the other corner. He said: It is not befitting for him to do that. But if there is a span's width between them, it suffices him.
He said: And I asked him about a man and a woman accompanying each other in a carriage, praying together. He said: No, but the man should pray first. So when he has prayed, the woman prays.

key_terms.يَتَزَامَلَانِ: accompanying each other / sharing the load

ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for a husband and wife praying together in the same room or carriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the spatial and temporal arrangements for marital prayer, emphasizing modesty through physical separation; it specifies that while a minimal distance (a span) may suffice in a confined corner, simultaneous prayer is discouraged in favor of sequential prayer to avoid distraction. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining distinct spiritual focus (khushu') while preserving the social decorum of the household. The preference for the man praying first also aligns with the general principle of the husband's leadership in family rituals.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked himasws about the man who is praying Salāt in a corner of the room, and his wife or his daughter is praying Salāt by his side in the other corner. So heasws said: ‘That is not befitting for him. But if there was one palm’s width (of distance between the two, so it would suffice him’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about the man and the woman accompanying each other in the carriage, praying Salāt together. So heasws said: ‘No, but the man should pray Salāt (first). So when he has prayed, the woman would pray Salāt’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked one of the two Imam, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about a man who performs Salah (prayer) in one corner of the room and his wife or daughter parallel with him in another corner of the room. He (the Imam) said, ‘He should not do so. If there is a distance of one shibr between them it is enough for him.’
I asked him (the Imam) about a man and woman share ride in a carriage and perform Salah (prayer) at the same time. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, man performs Salah (prayer) first, then the woman.’”
